answers.answer: Each player takes twelve ordinary turns: the 16 spaces are four seasons of three ordinary rounds plus a courtship. A courtship has no player turns, service rotation, monument income, or Servants’ Hall use.
answers.evidence: Overview: ‘each player takes twelve ordinary turns’; Turn Structure: courtship has ‘no ordinary turn or ongoing income.’

answers.answer: Hosting order: rotate Quarters to Available, then Expended to Quarters; resolve the round event; resolve applicable monument and Servants’ Hall effects; choose an activity; invite the exact required gentry; provide required service; resolve all positive favours before negative favours; optionally buy; clean up by sending used servants to Expended, played gentry to personal discard, and the activity tile back to its tableau column, flipping/upgrading as required. Only the last player advances the marker after cleanup.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure > Hosting an activity and Player Reference.

answers.answer: Pass order: all servants directly to Available; all gentry in personal discard to hand; round event then ongoing tile effects; choose £200 or a free full Market refresh; optionally buy one tile; last player advances the marker. Butler’s Room hiring is an activity, not a passing benefit. The two passing benefits are £200 or Market refresh.

Yes. The activity is screened using the reputation level fixed at the end of step 2, so 6.1 qualifies for PR6 even if four Service Help actions later lower actual reputation to 3.4. Service Help moves one servant per action from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service; it cannot take one directly from Expended Service. The tile and guests are screened at 6.1.
answers.evidence: Reputation screening is fixed at the end of step 2; Service Help costs and movement are stated in the special actions table.

answers.answer: Resolve all positive favours before all negative favours; within those groups their order is your choice. At minimum reputation, you cannot take a negative reputation favour first to shelter yourself from the loss; losses cannot go below 1.1. A money penalty must be fully payable: use positive activity money favours, a money VP card, or Borrow Money; if unable to fund it, you cannot play that guest/tile.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 6; Reputation, wealth and special actions: ‘A money penalty must be fully payable’ and minimum is 1.1.

answers.answer: Borrow Money costs 2 reputation increments and gains £100; repeatable. Service Help costs 3 increments per servant and moves one servant from Quarters to Available; repeatable. Refresh Market costs 4 increments for a full refresh; this special action is limited to once per turn. At minimum reputation you cannot take a special action. Service Help cannot take a servant directly from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Special actions table and minimum-reputation rule.

answers.answer: Host Servant Hiring using Butler’s Room, with an available butler or underbutler and no gentry. Take up to two Servants for Hire, excluding underbutlers, into Expended Service; there is no hiring fee. Once upgraded, instead you may recruit one common footman, valet, or lady’s maid from any location on one opponent’s family board into your Expended Service. No gentry may attend the base activity.

A housekeeper may substitute for a lady’s maid only when no lady’s maids are available. With a Brushing Room in your tableau, a footman may substitute for a valet only when no valets are available. An underbutler may substitute for any base male servant (butler, valet, footman), even if that servant type is available.

Acquire an underbutler only by purchasing Butler’s Pantry; it enters Expended Service immediately. Normally it moves to Quarters at your next service rotation and to Available Service at your second subsequent rotation; passing or Refresh Service VP card can make it available earlier, and once in Quarters Service Help or Servants’ Quarters can permit earlier use. Another player cannot recruit it because it is unique, not common.

Market price is the market-space price plus the tile’s printed price modifier; Reserve base price is £300 plus the modifier. The price cannot go below £100. You cannot acquire a duplicate you already own. Reputation does not restrict purchasing, so a tile above your reputation can be bought.

When a Market space becomes empty, slide remaining tiles left and draw replacements into rightmost spaces. A duplicate drawn stacks on its matching Market tile and another tile is drawn; stacked duplicates share one space and price. A Reserve-eligible draw goes directly to Reserve and you draw again. If several spaces are being filled, sort only the new tiles by sorting number. Buying one tile from a two-tile stack leaves the space occupied, so there is no refill.

After courtship 1, move Market Service tiles except Largest Wine Cellar to Reserve; later drawn Service tiles also go directly there, with the same exception. After courtship 2, move Market PR1 tiles to Reserve and later PR1 draws go there too. Largest Wine Cellar never enters Reserve. A full Market refresh after each of the first three courtships is standard, after Reserve movement.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve > Open Reserve and Refresh; Courtship and seasonal upkeep.

answers.answer: At an ordinary courtship, first return both Fairchilds to Alderley Hall. Highest score in the current theme category receives one VP card and chooses one Fairchild for hand; tied highest players each draw a VP card and no one gets a Fairchild. Each player discards one secret objective; shuffle simultaneous discards together and put them on the bottom of the objective deck. Then the first-player marker passes anticlockwise.

Final courtship scores tile VP for all four revealed themes (repeated categories count again). Highest gets one VP card and a Fairchild; reputation level breaks a tie, with wheel position ignored. If still tied, no Fairchild is awarded and tied winners draw VP cards under the tie rule. Discard the final objective. Then players have a final chance to use special actions and VP cards for benefits before scoring.

End-game VP comes from face-up improvement-tile VP (including negative and unused tiles); gentry VP in hand and discard (including negatives, family, final Fairchild); fulfilled remaining objectives; reputation levels 1–7 = 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28 VP; 2 VP per servant; wealth at 1 VP per £200 rounded down; and retained unused VP-card VP. The summary gives victory ties as final Fairchild, then highest reputation level, then shared victory. It does not state a complete multi-step tiebreak sequence beyond those rules. Wheel position does not affect reputation VP or final game tie resolution. Wealth rounding is down.
answers.evidence: Final VP table and final victory paragraph.

answers.answer: Normally receive five objectives at setup and two more on round 6. Discard one at each of four courtships, leaving three to score, plus any additional retained objectives earned from Main Library or an Objective VP card; these extras do not cause extra discards. Simultaneous discards are shuffled together before being placed face down on the objective deck bottom. Tile objectives require owning the named tiles at game end, not upgraded sides.

A VP card can be used immediately when drawn, at any time on your own later turn (multiple cards allowed), and once more after final courtship before scoring. Reveal and discard it when using its benefit; used cards go to the bottom of the VP deck. Retained unused cards stay hidden with objectives and score their printed VP; you cannot take both benefit and VP.

A normal activity tile must flip to its rose/upgrade side after its first use; an already-upgraded normal tile stays that way. Hybrids start with the underlined category showing and flip after every use. A tile that upgrades into an ongoing monument (Queen’s Suite or Lionheart Suite) hosts once, upgrades, and cannot host again. For hybrids only the face-up category counts at courtship and for objectives.

Monuments give one reputation per ordinary turn during ongoing effects, on hosting or passing; no income occurs during courtship, and a newly purchased monument first pays on a later turn. Servants’ Hall is resolved during ongoing effects on hosting or passing: place any one available servant on it, reduce one opponent’s reputation by one and gain one reputation; that servant cannot serve the activity and goes to Expended Service at turn end. You cannot target a player at minimum reputation.

Heritage Guest Suite uses one footman on the tile and one casual guest from hand, with that guest’s normal service; double all guest favours, including negative ones, and it remains an activity tile after upgrading. Queen’s Suite uses a housekeeper and one prestige guest from hand, with normal guest service; double one chosen favour and resolve others normally; upgrades into a monument. Lionheart Suite uses a butler and draws one prestige guest from the deck to attend, with no personal guest service; double nonnegative favours, keep the guest and put it in discard at cleanup; upgrades into a monument. All three have a fixed count of one guest; it cannot be changed.
answers.evidence: Suite activity table and following paragraph.

answers.answer: A random player gets the first-player marker. Starting to that player’s left and going clockwise, each player chooses an available base family board. Bonuses: Asquith adds the Dowager Countess as a fifth family card; Cavendish starts at reputation 1.4; Ponsonby gains £300; York adds a footman to Available Service.

Each player gets reputation counters 1/2, 3/4, 5/6 and Max with 1 showing and Max at the bottom; do not use 7/8. Starting reputation after family bonuses is Cavendish 1.4 and all others 1.1. Each gets a butler, housekeeper, valet, lady’s maid and footman in Available Service; five starter tiles (Private Study, Butler’s Room, Main Gazebo, Front Parlour, Bowling Green) with starter/building icon showing; and Lord, Lady, Heir and Young Lady family cards. Asquith has the extra Dowager; Ponsonby starts with £300; others have no money. York’s bonus footman is additional.

For three players, stock one valet and one lady’s maid per player (3 each), two footmen per player (6), and two underbutlers total. No butlers or housekeepers are stocked. Unused servants returned to the box are unavailable for the game.

Shuffle starter guests separately from the casual deck and deal two to each player’s hand; shuffle every undealt starter back into the casual deck. Starter guests are casual guests with a starter icon and otherwise follow normal casual rules; they are not a separate guest type during play.

For four players, select one double-sided monument per player plus one, so five. Choose at most one of Sculpture Garden and Garden Maze. Tiles that later upgrade into monuments always go in the bag and do not count against this selection. The setup states to put selected monuments and all nonstarter base improvement tiles in the bag, so later monument-upgrade tiles are in the bag.

Fill six different eligible Market spaces with tiles of PR3 or less (including no PR), excluding Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments. Set ineligible draws aside and return them after filling; stack duplicate eligible tiles in the same space. Normal tiles enter with upgrade/rose icon hidden and hybrids with underlined hybrid icon showing. Sort the six spaces by ascending sorting number starting at £300. PR4 tiles, Servants’ Hall, and double-sided monuments are ineligible.

Put Alderley Hall standard side up, round marker at 1, and one reminder token per player above the track. Shuffle theme and VP decks separately; reveal the first theme, which is open courtship, and keep revealed themes in order through the game. Put base Charles and Elizabeth Fairchild cards face up on Alderley Hall. Thus the first theme is not hidden and prior themes remain revealed.

At hosting-turn rotation, the servant in Quarters moves to Available Service; the servant in Expended Service moves to Quarters. Each advances one space. An available servant not used remains available.

No immediate Fair reward: the Study must already be upgraded when the event is resolved, before choosing/hosting the activity. An upgraded Private Study gives £300 and 2 reputation. Village Fair is on standard spaces 3 and 9.
answers.evidence: Round-track event table; Improvements > Private Study.

answers.answer: On round-track space 6, resolve Draw Objectives before ongoing tile effects; draw two and keep both secret with your other objectives. It is resolved on each player’s turn, including a pass, because events happen during both hosting and passing.
answers.evidence: Round-track events and event timing in Turn Structure.

answers.answer: Yes. During National Holiday, ignore PR on all tiles and guests when hosting. All other requirements remain, including service and gentry counts/types.

On Builders’ Holiday, buy any number from Market and/or Reserve within your funds. Complete purchases from the same unchanged market at the prices applying before the buying sequence; do not slide/refill between purchases or refresh between them with a special action or VP card. Refill all resulting empty spaces together after purchases. Market Purchase VP-card benefit follows the same Builders’ Holiday rules.
answers.evidence: Round-track table; Builders’ Market and Reserve > Builders’ Holiday / Market Purchase VP card.

answers.answer: For a full Market refresh, set all Market tiles aside, keep Reserve unchanged, refill all six spaces under normal refill rules, then return the set-aside tiles to the bag and mix. Set-aside tiles cannot reappear in that refresh. Reserve tiles stay as they were.

Each reputation symbol is one increment; move clockwise to gain and anticlockwise to lose. Crossing position 5 to 1 raises a level; crossing 1 to 5 lowers a level. Standard minimum is 1.1 and maximum is 7.5 (Max.5); losses beyond minimum are ignored. At Max.5, excess reputation is lost unless spent immediately on special actions; you may take actions before or during resolving a reputation favour to make room.

Money held is public, and players may not give or receive money between them. Never spend more than you have. The money supply is unlimited; use proxies if needed. The summary does not separately address whether a money cost may exceed holdings as a general rule, but does say a money penalty must be fully payable and Borrow Money may be used if possible.
answers.evidence: Reputation, wealth and special actions: money is public, supply unlimited, no player transfers; money penalty must be fully payable.

answers.answer: For a ladies requirement, any female family member or female guest qualifies; for gentlemen, any male family member or male guest qualifies. Casual-guest requirements require casual guests and exclude family. You must meet exactly the printed number and types, with no extras. Family members require no personal service and have no PR; the tile and played guests still follow reputation screening, while family cards have no PR.

An ordinary guest invite draws the indicated new guest card, reveals it to everyone, and adds it to your hand; the ordinary nonscreening symbol draws one card. For screening, draw the stated number, choose the stated number to keep, reveal only kept cards and add them to hand; put rejected cards on the bottom of their guest deck without revealing them.

Dismissal is optional. You may dismiss an eligible guest from hand, the current activity, or discard, including one just drawn earlier in the favours step. Family cannot be dismissed. Put the guest on the bottom of its matching deck; it is no longer yours, will not return when passing, and does not score VP.

Lord gives £200. Lady lets you choose either screening two casual guests and keeping one, or optionally dismissing one guest. Heir lets you choose £100 or one reputation. Asquith Dowager gives both £100 and one reputation. Thus Lady and Heir offer choices; Dowager gives both benefits.

The admirer bonus applies only with a male prestige guest attending the same activity. A male casual guest and a female prestige guest do not qualify; Charles Fairchild qualifies because he is a male prestige guest. The bonus is two reputation. The Young Lady still draws one casual guest in every case.
answers.evidence: Base family card table and Charles Fairchild clarification.

answers.answer: Both are prestige guests with no PR. Charles is male and requires a valet; his favour is three reputation. Elizabeth is female and requires a lady’s maid; her favour is one prestige guest and two reputation. They are guests, not family, so neither has family dismissal immunity and either may be dismissed under the normal rule.
answers.evidence: Gentry section and Fairchild favour description.

answers.answer: Miss Elizabeth Perkins reduces one opponent by one reputation. Miss Florence Oliver reduces one opponent by two and you lose one reputation. Minimum-reputation protection applies: a player at 1.1 cannot be targeted by an opponent’s reputation-reducing effect.
A Barn gives one reputation each time you host an Estate activity. Merely owning an Estate tile or passing gives no reputation.

Ordinary rotation moves all Quarters servants to Available, then all Expended servants to Quarters, each one space, at the start of a hosting turn. Servants’ Quarters lets you use one servant still in Quarters after rotation directly, in addition to Available, each ordinary turn, without reputation cost; that servant goes to Expended at turn end. Service Help instead costs 3 reputation increments per servant to move one Quarters servant to Available and cannot take directly from Expended.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring service mechanism table.

answers.answer: The front Private Study requires two family and a butler, with no tile favour. After its first use it upgrades permanently to an ongoing tile; it cannot be hosted again. Its upgraded side gives £300 and two reputation on Village Fair rounds without staffing or hosting it.

Before upgrading, Main Library uses a butler and two family and draws one extra objective. After upgrading, it uses a butler and three family and draws one VP card. Extra objectives increase the number retained for final scoring; they do not trigger an extra courtship discard.
answers.evidence: Improvements > Main Library; Objectives and VP cards.

answers.answer: The Objective VP card draws two objectives, keeps one, and returns the other to the bottom of the objective deck. It gives one additional retained objective for final scoring.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table; Objectives and VP cards.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Service moves all servants, including those in Expended Service, directly to Available Service, usable immediately. Service Help costs 3 reputation increments per servant and moves one servant only from Quarters to Available, never directly from Expended.

A Hire Servant VP card takes one servant from Servants for Hire, excluding underbutlers, into Expended Service. Because it is in Expended Service, it does not immediately provide service through normal Available Service; the summary does not specify any exception allowing immediate service from that destination.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table; servants in Expended are moved to Quarters by rotation.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Guest can return any one gentry, including a family member, from personal discard to hand. If used before Invite Gentry, you may choose that returned card to attend the current activity subject to normal requirements; returning to hand alone does not play it.

The basic-servant objective counts common footmen, valets and lady’s maids only; it excludes butler, housekeeper and underbutler. Ordinary service scoring gives 2 VP for every servant of all types and locations. The ten-servant objective gives 7 VP for at least ten servants total.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference and Final VP table.

answers.answer: Yes. Upgraded Queen’s Suite counts both as a monument and as an Estate tile; upgraded Lionheart Suite counts as a monument and as a Prestige tile. Thus each counts for both its category objective and the monument objective. A hybrid counts only in its currently face-up category.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference and Improvements; monument objective clarification.

answers.answer: Nature Group is worth 11 VP and requires Flower Room plus one of English Garden, French Garden, Sculpture Garden, or Garden Maze. Domestic Group is worth 12 VP and requires Gabled Conservatory plus one of Main Library or North Library. Ownership at game end suffices; use or upgrading is unnecessary.

The prestige-guest objective gives 1 VP per prestige guest. The every-three-guests objective counts all nonfamily guests, including prestige guests and a final Fairchild; incomplete groups of three score nothing. The summary explicitly says guests exclude family and Fairchild is a prestige guest.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference; Gentry section; guest objective definitions.

answers.answer: The reputation objective earns 7 VP for reaching maximum level 7, regardless of wheel position. The wealth objective earns 10 VP for at least £1200. Ordinary reputation VP is based on level only, and wheel position does not change reputation VP or reputation tie resolution.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference; Final VP and tie rules.

answers.answer: Both West Terrace sides require one butler and exactly three family cards. Before upgrading, its favour is to draw one prestige guest. After upgrading, draw one prestige guest and optionally dismiss one to four guests from hand, current activity, or discard to the bottoms of their decks. It remains an activity tile on both sides; it does not become an ongoing dismissal tile.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects > West Terrace.

answers.answer: There is no hand or discard-pile limit. Gentry in your discard pile remain yours and score normally.

You may inspect all Reserve tiles at any time and buy any one, including a tile underneath another in a stack; there is no top-tile-only restriction. Every Reserve tile is public and available for selection.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve > Open Reserve.

answers.answer: You are not required to host when able. Choose to host or pass. If required gentry or service are unavailable, choose another legal activity or pass; if no activity is possible, you must pass.

Yes. On a passing turn you may take the free Market refresh benefit, also use one paid special-action Market refresh, and use multiple Market Refresh VP cards in the same turn. The once-per-turn limit applies only to the paid special-action refresh; the other refresh methods have separate availability.
answers.evidence: Special actions and passing refresh rules.

answers.answer: No, these actions are not interrupts during another player’s turn. Special actions are available at any time on your own turn, hosting or passing, if you can afford the reputation cost.

No. Favours are mandatory unless expressly optional, so you cannot decline a printed ordinary guest invite just to avoid a draw while taking other favours. An optional dismissal may be declined; dismissal is always optional and removes an eligible guest from your ownership by bottom-decking it.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 6: favours mandatory unless expressly optional; Gentry: dismissal always optional.
